items.reason: The claim does not hold as written: the caps of the steps after the 80-minute clock allow the job to run past 110 minutes. The caps and clock checks the item names were applied so the job ends inside the cap. If the owner wants only the explanation, this change can be reverted.
items.evidence: The claim does not hold. On the file as the integrator left it, the steps after the 80-minute clock (JOB_START + 4800) had these caps and no clock guard (their guards were only the build outcome or the fetch): landmark check 3 min, landmark mark 5, terrain check 6, terrain mark 5, base map check 6, base map mark 5, manifest check 10, pack 5, publish 10. Worst paths by caps alone: landmark path 80 + 0.5 (kill grace) + 3 + 5 + 10 + 5 + 10 = 113.5 min; terrain path (or base map path) 80 + 0.5 + 6 + 5 + 10 + 5 + 10 = 116.5 min; with A3's 16-minute check the terrain path is 126.5 min. Each build's CAP is computed before its restore step (restore cap 10 min), so each path also gains that restore time. The publish's renames could also be cut by the job cap mid-way. Change applied: nine clock steps read JOB_START + 6300 (105 minutes). Checks and marks run only with more than 60 seconds left, and their programs run under timeout with CAP = min(static cap, time left). The manifest check (600 s), pack (300 s) and publish (600 s) start only when their whole cap fits before 105 minutes (guards above 600, 300 and 600). Builds keep the 80-minute clock (they end by about 90.5 min at most); verify keeps its guard (it ends by about 84 min). So every step ends by 105 minutes plus at most the 30-second kill grace: the last step ends by about 105.5 minutes, 4.5 minutes under the cap. Pins: test_the_monthly_end_clock_reads_105_minutes_and_keeps_five_minutes_under_the_cap; test_the_manifest_check_the_pack_and_the_publish_start_only_when_their_whole_cap_fits_before_the_monthly_end; test_the_checks_and_marks_after_the_monthly_clock_run_for_the_time_left_and_within_their_caps; test_every_step_after_the_monthly_clock_names_the_clock_it_waits_for. Also checked: all 26 step ids referenced by monthly conditions exist; bash -n passes on the 33 monthly run blocks; the CAP arithmetic clamps as intended for time-left values from 61 to 2000 seconds.
